subject: Physics
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate, never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic while practice support is routed separately.

must_contain: Explicit effort/input and load/output sides for one machine state.
An ideal force-distance tradeoff showing why force advantage does not create work.
A real-machine boundary case showing that losses can make input work exceed useful output work without introducing an efficiency formula.

controlled_variation.hold: the same useful output work in the ideal lossless model
controlled_variation.notice: a smaller effort force requires a larger effort distance

controlled_variation.vary: model from ideal lossless to real lossy
controlled_variation.notice: exact input-work = useful-output-work is an ideal-model equality, not a guarantee for real machines

controlled_variation.vary: whether the machine changes direction only or also force magnitude
controlled_variation.notice: machine usefulness is broader than force multiplication

must_contain: Load force divided by effort force, with both values from the same machine state.
A dimensionless-unit check and an interpretation of MA = 1 and MA > 1.

controlled_variation.notice: mechanical advantage changes as the load-to-effort ratio

controlled_variation.hold: the same numerical load and effort forces
controlled_variation.notice: MA is a generic force ratio independent of the machine name

must_contain: A lever, pulley and inclined-plane setup all described using effort/load input-output language.
A fixed-pulley counterexample to the claim that every useful machine reduces force magnitude.

controlled_variation.notice: different machines can change force magnitude, force direction or input distance in different combinations

controlled_variation.vary: the setup of the same machine type
controlled_variation.notice: the device name alone does not determine mechanical advantage

family.invariant_demand: Identify effort and load sides for the same machine state, decide what changes about force/direction/distance, distinguish ideal lossless tradeoffs from real losses, and only then interpret mechanical advantage.
family.difficult_move: Seeing force advantage as a modelled input-output tradeoff rather than energy creation, while not overextending the ideal work equality to every real machine.
family.independent_check: MA must be dimensionless and use load/effort from the same state; an ideal force advantage requires a compensating distance tradeoff; a real lossy machine may need more input work than useful output work.

support_ladder.handed_over: Effort/load sides and the relevant tradeoff are labelled.
Effort and load sides are labelled.
Only the real-world machine setup is supplied.

transfer.changed_demand: An unfamiliar workshop tool must be analysed as a generic effort/load machine without being named as a lever, pulley or incline.
A fixed pulley changes force direction but not magnitude, requiring the learner to reject the assumption that all useful machines have MA > 1.
A force advantage is given and the learner must infer the compensating distance tradeoff before calculating or claiming an energy gain.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: which input/output distances complete the work ledger
